Introduction
Introduction
About HyperSense
Last updated on May 12, 2023
HyperSense is an Artificial Intelligence (AI) automation platform that provides all the capabilities of 
data analytics, data science and insight generation in one solution. It democratizes AI across the da‐
ta value chain that allows business users to easily unify data from disparate sources, automate te‐
dious and complex data science processes and turn the data into insights through auto visualization. 
It leverages AI-driven decision analytics and widens access to data, data science, artificial intelli‐
gence (AI), and machine learning (ML) to anyone in an organization. 
In the recent years, many organizations in the industry have addressed the following issues, and Hy‐
perSense helps them overcome the same:
Siloed Data: Data is siloed in many sections and is not accessible across the organization. Unify‐
ing the data from disparate sources enables business users to access the data from a central‐
ized repository providing a single source-of-truth.
1.
Monolith Architecture: Existing enterprise systems built on monolith architecture makes integra‐
tion with other systems difficult. HyperSense platform is built on a data fabric driven micro ser‐
vices architecture which allows easy integration with new systems, build tenant use cases on it, 
and with fail fast mechanisms, explores new uses quickly.
2.
Data Collaboration: Existing system makes the collaboration of data between business users, IT 
users, and data scientists difficult. So centralized data lake and a unified Process Automation 
system allow users from across organizational boundaries to collaborate and communicate is‐
sues across complex workflows.
3.
Domain Orientation: Existing enterprise tools lack domain components. HyperSense platform 
provides business users with pre-built domain use cases and the ability to extend the use cases 
to the various domain.
4.
Data Preparation: Data discovery and manual data preparation used to take a lot of time for data 
scientists and data engineers. With augmented data discovery and data preparation, business 
users quickly understand the nature of data, its features, and lineage that result in quicker de‐
ployment of use cases and insights.
5.
AI Practitioners: There is a lack of AI practitioners with deep learning backgrounds. The aug‐
mentation of AI in the HyperSense platform allows business users to try AI/ML experiments 
without specialized skillsets and yet derive value for the business.
6.

Last updated on May 12, 2023
Data Catalog is a centralized repository that contains detailed information about the data sources, 
datasets, and other relevant metadata in HyperSense. It helps you to search for required data table 
and view the data in it to perform data operations such as Data Filtering, Data Import, Data Export, 
Data Share, etc. You can create a table and insert a row, edit or delete an existing row, and truncate 
the table manually using CRUD operations. Data Catalog serves as a catalog or inventory for the 
datasets that are coming from ETL pipelines, Streaming and Batch pipelines of HyperSense.
1. Source of Incoming Data in Data Catalog

2. Data Exploration in Data Catalog

From ETL Pipeline: In ETL pipeline process, after creating a pipeline and configuring the data 
source, transformation operator and data sink, the pipeline is scheduled, deployed and Run. After 
you successfully run the pipeline, the data from the data sinks is loaded into the database. The 
data from the sinks which is in the format of RDBMS and S3presto tables is visible in Data Catalog.

From Streaming and Batch Pipelines: In Streaming and Batch pipeline process, after creating a 
pipeline, configuring the data reader, transformation operator and data sink, the pipeline is sched‐
uled and Run. After you successfully run the pipeline, the resultant output data is stored in the 
sinks and the preview from the sinks like RDBMS, S3 external, GCP external, Azure external can 
be viewed in data catalog.
•
From CRUD Operations: CRUD operations are the basic operations that a Data Catalog can per‐
form on a data table. CRUD operations allow you to Insert, Edit, Delete the records in a row 
and Truncate the table. This helps you manually create new records, view the existing records, 
modify the existing records, and remove the records from data table.

3. Data Operations in Data Table
After accessing a data table, following are the data operations that you can perform:
Dataset Export/Import: Data Catalog allows you to search for a dataset using search bar at the top 
of dataset listing page and perform Dataset Export/Import. This helps you to export any dataset 
from one instance (source client) and import the exported dataset to another instance (destination 
client). For more information on how to search a dataset and perform import/export operations, 
see Dataset Export and Import.
•
Create Table: Data Catalog provides a platform to create and collaborate among data assets. You 
can create a data table directly from the dataset listing page and add tags and comments to any 
dataset, facilitating the collaboration around data assets. For more information on how to create a 
table, filter datasets based on Tags, see Create Table.
•
Sort Datasets: Sort Datasets in data catalog allows you to sort the datasets as required. This helps 
you to provide improved readability and data analysis. For more information on how to sort 
datasets, see Sort Datasets.
•
Ageing: Ageing feature in data catalog allows you to clean up the partition table data for both Tri‐
no and Postgres tables by configuring the retention period (in days) for any dataset. This helps 
you to retain the required data without getting deleted. For more information on configuring age‐
ing, see Ageing.
•
Dataset View: Dataset View in data catalog allows you to access the schematic view of any 
dataset, create expandable link to view the specific records from a data table by accessing 
the expandable link, store cache data locally, and configure auto load option for datasets. For 
more information, see Dataset View.
•
Share Dataset: Share Dataset in data catalog helps you to share the dataset privileges to autho‐
rized user group(s) in HyperSense. It has access controls to ensure that sensitive data is accessi‐
ble only to authorized user group(s). It manages access permissions of who can view, search and 
share the datasets in order to avoid unauthorized access. For more information, see Share 
Dataset.
•
Data Table Search: Data Table Search allows you to search and view the data table from required 
dataset. It helps you to explore the data available in a specific data table. For more information on 
how to search and view the data in a data table, see Data Table Search.
•
Data Table Import and Export: Data Table Import allows you to import the data to a data table in 
CSV or XLS file formats. Data Table Export allows you to export the data present in a table in any 
of these formats: CSV, RTF, PDF and TEXT. Import and Export operations are used in a wide va‐
riety of contexts for different purposes such as Data Migration, Data Backup, Data Analysis, 
etc. For more information on how to import and export a data table, see Data Table Import and 
Export.
1.
Share Data Table: Share Data Table allows you to share the data table to the required user(s) 
and user group(s). Sharing a data table serves several important purposes such as Collabora‐
tion, Data Analysis, Decision Making, etc. For more information on how to share a data table, see 
Share Data Table.
2.

title: HyperSense User Guide
text:
Version:  2.5.13.5
© 2026 Subex - Confidential
Page 24
4. Data Catalog Integration
Overall, data catalog in HyperSense acts as a central repository for data knowledge, and leverage 
the data assets to enhance data driven decision making.
Table Settings: Table Settings in data catalog allows you to configure the data table grid view 
options like alignment, order, currency format and apply the color rules to the data table. For 
more information, see Table Settings.
3.
Data Filtering: Data Filtering is widely used to explore the specific data for analysis. It allows you 
to filter the required data based on the type of filter configured.
4.
To filter the specific data from a data table, you can use the following list of filters in Data 
Catalog:
a.
Basic Filter: Basic Filters allows you to filter and fetch the data in a data table based on the fil‐
ter values configured. For more information on basic filter, see Basic Filter. 
b.
Advanced Filter: Advanced Filter allows you to filter the records in a data table based on the 
expressions defined. For more information on advanced filter, see Advanced Filter.
c.
Filter based on Fx function: Fx function filter allows you to fetch the data from the data tables 
using predefined functions. For more information on Fx function filter, see Fx Function Func‐
tion.
d.
Date Selector Filter: Date Selector filter allows you to filter the data based on selected range 
of dates, relative time stamp values, and quick time intervals. For more information, see Date 
Selector.
e.
Link Analysis: Link analysis is a data analysis technique used to evaluate relationship (connec‐
tions) between the nodes. It allows you to transform the data in a data table in the form of link 
graphs. This helps you to analyse any complex data in a data table more easily. For more infor‐
mation, see Link Analysis.
5.
CRUD Operations: CRUD operations allow you to Insert, Edit, Delete the records in a row 
and Truncate the table in a data table. In data catalog, you can perform CRUD operations only on
RDBMS Oracle & RDBMS Postgres tables. For more information, see CRUD Operations.
6.
Data catalog can be integrated with Business Intelligence tool to visualize the data in the form of 
charts and dash boards. This integration enables seamless data discovery and access within the 
existing data ecosystem.
•
Data Catalog can be integrated with Business Modelling tool on which you can run queries. Query 
Measures provides data to Key Performance Indicators (KPIs). Key Performance Indicators (KPI) 
provides threshold settings for measures. The result of an individual KPI on a query measure can 
either be a Passed or Violated value. When a measure violates KPI, system generates an alert and 
then a case gets created.
•

Last updated on May 12, 2023
Date Selector allows you to filter the data based on selected range of dates, relative time stamp val‐
ues, and quick time intervals. Date Selector is available at top tool bar where you view the specific 
data table. Date selector option will be displayed only for partitioned tables.
Following types of filter categories available:
Note:
To configure Date Selector:
The Fx search bar is displayed. You can either enter the PIVOT function in search bar or enter 
space bar to select it from the drop-down. Enter the required Column name, function name and 
hit enter.
2.

Go back to Data Catalog page to know about date selector filter.
4.
Absolute: Allows you to fetch the records within the selected range (Start and End datetime). 
Time stamp format is MM/DD/YYYY HH:MM:SS. Select the From and To date.
Example: If the configured From date and time is 10/01/2016 12:00:00 AM and To date as 
10/3/2019 11:59:59 PM, it will fetch the records between 10/01/2016 12:00:00 AM and 
10/3/2019 11:59:59 AM.
•
Relative: Allows you to fetch the records based on the relative time stamp values.
Example: If the time period configured is 1000 minutes ago in the first field and 1 minute ago in the 
second field, then it will consider the From date as 1000 minutes before the current time stamp 
and To date as 1 minute before the current time stamp. In total, it will fetch the records for the 
time stamp values available between.
If we consider the current time stamp is 11/13/2020, then the records are fetched from 11/03/2020 
to 11/12/2020.
•
Quick: Allows you to fetch the records with the quick intervals. It can be the hours, days, weeks or 
years.
Example: If the configured time-stamp value is Last 10 days then it will fetch the records for last 
10 days from current date. If the configured time interval is last year, it will fetch the records for 
only the previous year.
If the configured interval is current day then it will fetch the records only for current day.

Record Duplicate
Last updated on January 21, 2026
This feature identifies and filters duplicate records present in a data table. It generates a hash code 
for each entry and compares hash code values to detect identical records. When duplicates are 
found, the system retains and processes the latest record according to configurable rules. This en‐
sures data consistency, optimizes storage, and improves processing efficiency.
Note:
This feature is available for Batch Pipelines in Business Modelling Studio. It supports both Query 
Measure and SQL Measure.
Prerequisite
The following prerequisites must be completed in the Data Management studio:

Common Actions on Dashboard
You can perform below actions on the dashboard charts:
Sources: Sources contains the list of all the data source available in Data Management Stu‐

sources . Select the data sources and Click on forward arrow icon to view details on charts.

is a dropdown field that is used as filter to display the details of selected data sinks. Select 
the data sinks and Click on forward arrow icon to view details on charts .
c.
Charts: Below are the list of charts available:
2.
Pipeline Status: This is a Donut chart that displays the pipeline status (like Deployed, Run‐
ning, Drafted, In-progress, or Failed) of the pipelines.
a.
Collections: This is a Donut chart that displays the data collection status (like Completed, In-
progress, and  Failed) of data received from data sources.
b.
Load and Sink: This is a bar chart that displays the total number of records accepted (loaded) 
and rejected(not loaded) into data sinks. X-axis has Pipeline Name, and Y-axis has Records 
Loaded and Records Rejected.
c.
Record Trend: This is a line chart that displays the number of records collected from data 
source for the selected data range. X-axis has Date Range and Y-axis has Records Loaded. 
Available options are Yearly, Quarterly, Monthly, Daily, Hourly, and None. Based on the se‐
lection, Record Trend chart visual is changed.
d.
Date wise File Trend: This is a multi-value chart that displays the total files collected per date 
for the selected date range. X-axis has Date, and Y-axis has Total Files.
e.
File Trend: This is a bar chart that displays the number of files collected in each pipeline from 
data source for the selected date range. X-axis has Total Files, and Y-axis has Pipeline 
Names.
f.
File Size(Out of Range): This is a multi-value chart that displays the count for number of files 
that exceeds minimum and maximum file size. X-axis has Timestamp, and Y-axis has Count 
for Files that are out of range. This chart works for following Data Source: Azure, FTP, GCS, 
SFTP, S3.
g.
Missing File Sequence: This is a multi-value chart that displays the count for number of files 
that are missing sequence. X-axis has Timestamp, and Y-axis has Count for Files Missing Se‐
quence.
h.
Transform: This is a Donut chart that displays the data transformation status (like Completed, 
In-progress, and Failed ) of data sources.
i.
Duplicate File: This is a bar chart that displays the number of duplicate files available in the 
source of the each pipeline. X-axis has Pipeline Name, and Y-axis has No of duplicate files.
j.
Slice: Apply filter on Pipelines, Source or Sinks to perform slice action. For example: In Pipelines, 
pipeline "VDS_PRM_Spcp_telemetry1_jan20" and "VDS_PRM_Tapout_telemetry1_jan20" is fil‐
tered. Slice is created for these two pipelines. All other charts are updated accordingly. If you

plied settings only after performing undo operation. It re-applies the removed filter again.

Audit Trail
Last updated on December 16, 2024
An Audit Trail refers to a chronological record of events or activities that provide a detailed account 
of changes or actions taken within a system, process, or organization. It is commonly used in the 
context of information technology systems and financial or regulatory compliance. Audit trail logs 
are essential for ensuring accountability, transparency, and security in various domains. They serve 
as a means of tracking and documenting critical activities, enabling organizations to review and vali‐
date the integrity of their operations. In HyperSense, audit trail window allows you to view the logs 
(API logs and Event logs) of all the actions performed in all windows.
The key aspects of Audit Trail 
& Successful logins from the chart.

Expired users from User Management Module. You can view the Count of Active & Blocked 
Users, and Percentage of Active & Blocked users from the chart.

Connections: Connection chart allows you to view the status of smsc and smtp connections 
which replicates the configured setup of SMS host and Email Server Information respectively in 
Common Settings page.
3.
API Call Trend: API Call Trend chart allows you to view the number of internal API calls available 
for a specific service available in HyperSense.
4.
Minio Disk Usage: Minio is a storage space. In Minio Disk Usage chart, you can view the infor‐
mation of Allocated Space, Available Space and Used Space for each server on a particular day.
5.
Postgres Disk Usage: In Postgres Disk Usage chart, you can view the information of Allocated 
Space, Available Space and Used Space for each server on a particular day.
6.
Recordkeeping: Audit trails maintain a comprehensive log of events, capturing details such as the 
date, time, user details, and specific actions performed. They can include activities such as log 
type, user details, user actions, message regarding user action.
•
Security and Compliance: Audit trails play a crucial role in security management and compliance 
with regulatory requirements. By tracking user actions and system activities, organizations can 
identify potential security breaches, unauthorized access, or policy violations.
•
Forensic Analysis: In the event of an incident or suspected wrongdoing, audit trails serve as valu‐
able forensic evidence. They allow investigators to reconstruct events, determine the sequence 
of actions, and identify individuals involved in unauthorized activities or data breaches.
•
Monitoring and Detection: Real-time monitoring of audit trails enables organizations to detect 
anomalies or suspicious behavior promptly. Automated systems can analyze the recorded data 
for patterns, deviations, or indicators of potential security threats.
•
Accountability and Transparency: Audit trails foster accountability by establishing a clear record 
of who performed specific actions and when. This transparency helps organizations identify re‐
sponsible parties for errors, omissions, or compliance violations.
•

systems or organizations. They promote accountability, security, compliance, and enable organiza‐
tions to monitor and analyze activities for various purposes.

troubleshoot errors. When problems arise, reviewing the audit trail can help identify the source of 
issues, revert unintended changes, and restore the system's integrity.

filteredsearch

Decimal Settings: Click the Decimal Settings checkbox to enable the decimal precision func‐

types.

required option either (,) Comma or (.) Dot.

when (.) Dot is used as thousand's separator, (,) Comma acts as Decimal Indicator.
◦
If you disable Thousand's Separator checkbox, the data will be displayed without any sep‐
arator.
◦
If you disable Decimal Settings, the decimal values will not be displayed.
◦

Sample number field and check the output in After Settings Applied field.

abled. Select the Use Single Currency checkbox to enable the Currency Format in configure

ger, Long, Double and Float as data types.

lect Australian dollar from Select Currency dropdown and click Update.

low.

columns.

limits the given sample number to three digits after decimal place and separates the sample 
number with comma for every thousand's digit. It will not round off the value when there is a 
number that is more than five.

Last updated on January 19, 2024

breach or deviation happens to the configured policy measures in HyperSense. Alerts are essential

If the selected entity is PAS, by configuring the policy, an alert is generated:
◦
Case Statistics - New Cases alert: If select period is configured as 15 minutes and if the 
Measures under Policy field is selected as New cases, the system validates if there are 
any new cases generated for selected period. If system detects any new cases in the 
defined time period, then it triggers an alert via configured communication channel and 
notification is sent to configured user(s) or Group(s).
•

title: HyperSense User Guide
text:
Version:  2.5.13.5
© 2026 Subex - Confidential
Page 134
Case Statistics - Available cases alert: If select period is configured as 15 minutes and if 
the Measures under Policy field is selected as Available cases, the system validates 
if there are any available cases exist for selected period. If system detects any available 
cases in the defined time period, then it triggers an alert via configured communication 
channel and notification is sent to configured user(s) or Group(s).
•
Case Statistics - Recurred cases alert: If select period is configured as 15 minutes and if 
the Measures under Policy field is selected as Recurred cases, the system validates if 
there are any recurred cases exist for selected period. If system detects any recurred 
cases in the defined time period, then it triggers an alert via configured communication 
channel and notification is sent to configured user(s) or Group(s).
•
Case Statistics - Cases in Pipeline alert: If you select this alert under the policy measure 
Case Statistics - Cases in Pipeline, and configure alert conditions, an alert is generated 
as per the configured alert condition and this helps user to know the number of cases 
per pipeline. 
This alert has the three variables: 
•
@Number_of_cases_per_pipeline: Provides the count of the cases for each pipeline. 
For example (simbox:2; irsf:1) where simbox, irsf represents Pipeline and 2,1 repre‐
sents the number of cases.
◦
@Pipeline_count: Provides the number of pipelines which has breached the alert poli‐
cy.
◦
 @Pipeline_names: Provides the name of pipelines which has breached the alert poli‐
cy
◦
Case Expiry Alert: While configuring any case template, user can set SLA for that case 
template. After case template configuration, when ever a case gets generated from 
BMS and if the SLA for that case is breached, then case gets expired. Whenever case 
gets expired, an email alert notification is sent to the current workstep owner notifying 
the case expiry.
Note:
User needs to enable email notification in workstep allocation tab while creating 
template to get this expiry mail alert.
•
If selected entity is SYSADMIN
 If the selected entity is Sys Admin, by configuring the policy, an alert is generated:
◦
If the Measure under Policy fields is selected as Incorrect User Login Report, and the 
select period is 1 hour, then the system validates if there are any failed user logins for 
the past 24 hours and then it triggers an alert after one hour via configured communica‐
tion channel and notification is sent to configured user(s) or Group(s).
•
If the Measure under Policy fields is selected as Logged Users Exceeded, and the select 
period is 1 hour, then the system validates if there are any logged users for the past one 
hour based on configured policy condition and then it triggers an alert after one hour via 
•

title: HyperSense User Guide
text:
Version:  2.5.13.5
© 2026 Subex - Confidential
Page 135
configured communication channel and notification is sent to configured user(s) or 
Group(s). For example, if you configure policy as Logged in Users Number > 10, then 
systems generates the alert only if the logged in users number is greater than 10.
If the Measure under Policy fields is selected as User Behavioural Report, and the select 
period is 1 hour, then the system validates the audit logs of the particular user for the 
past 24 hours and then it sends the report and triggers an alert after one hour via con‐
figured communication channel and notification is sent to configured user(s) or 
Group(s).
•
If the Measure under Policy fields is selected as Unauthorized API Call Report, and the 
select period is 1 hour, then the system validates if there are any unauthorized API Calls 
for the past 24 hors and  then it sends the report and triggers an alert after one hour via 
configured communication channel and notification is sent to configured user(s) or 
Group(s).
•
To configure policy, select the required measure from Measures dropdown. Upon select‐
ing the measure, the below options get auto populated to define the conditions required 
for the respective configuration.
◦
Select Variable Names: The Select Variable Names dropdown lists the variables re‐
lated to the selected measure. Select the required variable to define the policy con‐
figuration.
•
Select Operator: The Select Operator is the dropdown that provides the list of opera‐
tors to define the selected variable with its configuration values. Select the required 
operator from the Select Operator dropdown list to define the required condition.

quirement.

is defined in the configuration. You can combine the policies using the condition defined to 
it. To add new policy, click Add Policy option which auto populates the Select Variable 
Names, Select Operator, and Values fields for the current policy to be configured. You can 
add any number of policies as required.

policies with Conditional AND, Conditional OR options. Enter the required condition 
from Conditions drop down.
•
If you select and condition, then an alert is triggered only when both the de‐
fined rules in conditional expression are true.
•
 If you select or condition, then an alert is triggered when any one of the de‐
fined rule in conditional expression is true.
•
Remove Policy: This option helps you to remove the current policy and its subse‐
quent rules configured. Click Remove Policy to remove the current policy. Remove 
Policy is populated only when two or more policies are added under Add Policy sec‐
tion.

Error Logging
Overview
Last updated on January 19, 2024
An Error Logging is error dashboard that is a centralized location where you can monitor, analyse, 
and troubleshoot the errors that have occurred in Hypersense. The error logging dashboard has er‐
ror statistics and a display pane. Error Statistics is a graphical representation of different errors and 
error trends for a particular duration. Display Pane displays error details such as error occurence 
date and time, log level for error, error type, studios, and associated services where error has oc‐
curred, and description of the error.
You can navigate to error logging page using either of the ways:
Workspace
Workspace of Error Dashboard has various icons, graphs and display pane.
You will find below details on the page:
From Common Left Panel, Admin > Error Logging.
1.
From Home Page, Click expand icon of System Administration > Error Logging.
2.
Top Right Corner Icon: These icons are present at the top right-hand side corner. 
1.
Page Refresh: It allows you to view the latest log without removing the filters applied. Click 
the refresh icon to refresh the page and view the latest logs.
a.
Settings: It allows you to configure Error Statistics and Error Configuration.
b.
Error Statistics: It is a toggle switch. Click to display or hide the Errors and Error Trend 
graphs. For more information, refer to Error Statistics Details.
i.
Error Configuration: It allows you to configure the error setting of the available services 
for DMS, BMS, Sysadmin and PAS studios. Error Configuration has different log level such 
as Debug, Info, Warning, Error. Click the toggle switch to enable the log levels.
Note:
 
ii.
By default, Error log option is enabled and cannot be disabled.
•
For example: If Debug log is enabled, log levels - Info and Warning log are enabled 
automatically and cannot be disabled. Similarly, If Info log is enabled, Warning log 
is enabled automatically and cannot be disabled. 
•
For example: If Debug log is disabled, Info and Warning log are disabled automati‐
cally. Similarly, If you want to enable Warning log, Click the toggle switch. In case 
you enable Info log, Warning log also gets enabled.
•
i-icon: Upon clicking the i-icon, it allows you to navigate to the help file of the error logging 
dashboard. You can learn about its functionality.
c.

Let us consider a ETL pipeline flow in DMS where the data flow is from SFTP (Source) to S3 presto

Task Search
Last updated on February 18, 2026
Task Search is introduced to capture the information associated with pipeline from the Business 
Modelling Studio (BMS) and Data Management Studio (DMS). This screen displays the information 
such as pipeline name, studio name, start and end time, pipeline version, pipeline status, action sta‐
tus, look-back start time, look-back end time, and modified time. Whenever any pipeline is created in 
BMS or DMS, its reference is captured in Task Search Dashboard.
Note:
Functionality Access
It allows you to access the task search screen. Check below steps to configure functionality access.
To access task search screen, make sure you have Task Search functionality access.
•
To perform actions on pipeline, make sure you have Pipeline functionality access such as cre‐
ate, edit, delete and so on.
•
Steps to configure functionality access
•
Create User and User Group > assign user to the user group. For more information, see Cre‐
ate New User and Create New User Group.
1.
Find the user group using the search bar.
2.
Select the User Group > Click the vertical ellipsis > Click Functionality Access.
3.
Task Search - Functionality Access window is displayed. It displays the list of the services 
and related microservices.
4.
Perform action: Select Sysadmin Tab > Select ITOPs services from the microservice list > Se‐
lect ITOPs service.
5.

formation, access to home page, and access to help document.

the screen. Below is the list of actions:
3.
On Task Filters: It allows you to select the options from the drop-down list. Below are the 
available drop-down option:
a.
Studio: It displays the list of studios, whose pipeline actions are displayed. The available 
studios are BMS and DMS.
i.
Type: It displays the entity type. The available entity type is Pipeline.
ii.
Status: It displays the list of pipeline statuses available in the studios. Few of the pipeline 
statuses are Deployed, Failed, Killed, Drafted, Finished, Running, Deleted, and so on.
iii.
How to apply filter using drop-down
iv.
Click the drop-down icon.
1.
Select the checkbox of the required option.
2.
Once an option is selected, data is populated as per the selected option.
3.
Date Filter: It displays the pipeline details as per the selected date range. Below are the avail‐
able date ranges:
b.
1D: Displays the pipeline details from the current time minus 24 hours. For example, the 
current date and time is 24-03-2025 17:17:00. Then 1D will display pipeline details from 
23:03:2025 17:17:00 to 24-030-2025 17:17:00.
i.

ii.

iii.

iv.
6M: Displays the pipeline details for the past 6 months from the current day.
v.
1Y: Displays the pipeline details for the past year from the current day.
vi.
Total: Displays complete pipeline details present in the system.
vii.
Custom: You can view the pipeline details for customized dates. Select the Start Date/
Time, and End Date/Time. Click Save.
viii.
Refresh: It refresh the data. The snackbar message is displayed "Data refreshed successful‐
ly."
c.

able in the studio. It acts as a filter. When you click any operational card, pipeline details are dis‐
played in the display pane, and the quick access toolbar is updated accordingly.
4.
Search Bar: It allows you to search the pipeline/entity name. Auto-suggestion populates the 
pipeline name when you search a pipeline. It is not applicable on columns that accept data type 
as integer and date. For example: If you try to search using version number / start time / end 
time, result is not displayed.

success rate of the schedule tasks. For more information, see Task Schedule.
Note: By default, Schedule icon is disabled. Select the task to enable the icon.
a.

options are CSV, TXT, PDF, and RTF. After successful export, a snackbar message is dis‐
played: "Downloaded table data in the form of <selected option>."

Ageing
By default, task search has 180 days of retention period which runs daily at 12 am midnight. During 
cleanup activity task entries older than 180 days are removed, except for those which are in running 
state.
 
Task Schedule for BMS Batch Pipelines
Currently, if multiple pipelines are scheduled at same time, there is a possibility of pipeline failure 
due to limited resources. To address this, the Schedule option in Task Search has been introduced 
to maximize the success rate of the pipeline execution.
The system recommends future time slots by analyzing existing scheduled configurations. It calcu‐
lates the average execution time based on the last N successful runs, thereby minimizing overlaps, 
avoiding parallel executions, and reducing performance slowdowns.
Note:
 
To configure the Task Schedule, follow the steps below:
In Common Left Panel, Click Admin > Audit Trail.
1.
Audit Trail window is displayed.
2.
Look for Entity column.
3.
Click filter icon > Type TaskSearch > Click Apply.
4.
Result will display the Audit Logs captured.
5.
You can read the messages in Message column and track the task actions performed.
6.
By default, the interval between two consecutive schedules is 30 minutes.
•
You can schedule tasks for a maximum of 20 pipelines at a time.
•
Execution history must be available for any pipeline. If execution history is not available, the 
default suggestion will be the next schedule time.
•
The pipeline execution time is calculated as average of the last successful run. For example, if 
five runs took 12, 10, 11, 13, and 9 minutes respectively, the expected execution time will be 11 
minutes.
•
If multiple tasks of the same pipeline are selected for bulk scheduling, the system recom‐
mends different schedule times, even when resources are available. This prevents conflicts 
caused by multiple tasks attempting to update the same reporting table simultaneously.
•
If all time slots for a day are blocked, no schedule time is suggested. The scheduler remains 
empty, allowing users to schedule tasks as required.
•
When pipeline execution restarts, the pipeline moves to the Submitted State. After comple‐
tion, pipeline status is updated accordingly.

User Management
User Management
Overview
Last updated on June 17, 2023
User management refers to the processes and tools used by organizations to control and administer 
access to their systems, applications, and resources. Effective user management is crucial for main‐
taining security, compliance, and overall operational efficiency.
The key aspects of User Management are
User Authentication:
1.
Password Management: Ensuring strong password policies, including regular password up‐
dates, complexity requirements, and secure storage.
•
Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA): Adding an extra layer of security by requiring users to 
provide multiple forms of identification (e.g., password and mobile verification code).
•
User Provisioning:
2.
Onboarding: Creating user accounts for new employees and providing them with the neces‐
sary access rights and privileges.
•
Offboarding: Deactivating or deleting user accounts when employees leave the organization 
to prevent unauthorized access.
•
User Permissions and Roles:
3.
Role-Based Access Control (RBAC): Assigning roles to users based on their job responsibili‐
ties, allowing for easier management of permissions.
•
Granular Permissions: Configuring specific access rights for individual users or groups to en‐
sure the principle of least privilege.
•
User Monitoring and Auditing:
4.
Activity Logging: Keeping track of user activities, logins, and changes made to permissions 
for security and auditing purposes.
•
Regular Audits: Periodically reviewing and validating user permissions to ensure compliance 
and security.
•
Account Lockout and Recovery:
5.
Account Lockout Policies: Implementing measures to automatically lock out user accounts af‐
ter a certain number of failed login attempts to prevent unauthorized access.
•
Account Recovery: Providing mechanisms for users to regain access to their accounts in 
case of forgotten passwords or other issues.
•
Single Sign-On (SSO):
6.
Centralized Authentication: Allowing users to access multiple applications with a single set of 
credentials, enhancing user experience and reducing the need for multiple logins.
•

Visualize the Data
Business Intelligence (BI) refers to visualize the analysed data to derive actionable insights, tech‐
nologies, and strategies that organizations use to transform raw data into meaningful and actionable 
insights. It involves reading transformed data from Data Management/ Business Modeling and repre‐
senting the transform data in the form of charts and tables to support data-driven decision-making 
and improve overall business performance. By leveraging BI, organizations can gain a deeper under‐
standing of their operations, customers, market trends, and other relevant factors influencing their 
business success.
Reporting and visualization: BI tools enable the creation of reports, dashboards, and visualizations to 
present data in a clear and concise manner, facilitating better understanding and decision-
making. Refer the below graphic representation for work process of Business Intelligence.
By leveraging business intelligence, organizations can gain a competitive edge by identifying oppor‐
tunities, understanding customer behavior, optimizing operations, and making data-driven strategic 
decisions. It empowers stakeholders at all levels to access timely, relevant information, fostering a 
culture of data-driven decision-making within the organization. Refer the below graphic representa‐
tion for work process of Business Intelligence.
1. Create Dashboard
In Business Intelligence Home page, first step is to click on Create Dashboard icon. The connection 
refers to the process of establishing a link or interface between a BI tool or platform and a data 
source. This connection allows the BI tool to access, retrieve, and analyze data from the specified 
data source. To create connection choose the appropriate data source that contains the relevant da‐
ta for analysis. For more information, refer to Connect to Data Repository.
2. Add Data Source
The second step is to Add Data Source which helps you to fetch the data from the different sources 
like Database connection (Postgres,  Trino, S3Presto, S3), S3( Bucket Path) and CSV data import. By 
using the data source user can create interactive dashboards that allow users to create visualiza‐
tions tailored to their specific needs. Users can select relevant data, apply filters, and configure visu‐
al elements like charts, graphs. 
To add the datasource as per the source type, select the below Type:
3. Design
The third step, on the design page requires you to choose the added source to create a Visualization 
and then customize the organization, formatting, and styling of the report's visual elements, such as 
tables, charts, and graphs.
Design page refers to a work-space or interface within a BI tool where users can create and design 
various elements of their BI solution.

Blue: It means the data source is cached successfully. You can request for another cache refresh,

lowed.

data source caching status is completed.

DS3 are requested for caching. Now if you try to refresh dashboard D3, a snackbar mes‐
sage is displayed as "data source(s) is already in progress" .
◦
Case 2: Consider data sources DS1 and DS3 are cached successfully, whereas data 
source DS2 caching is in process. Now if you try to refresh dashboard D2, a snackbar 
message is displayed as "data source(s) is already in progress" .

For Example: Hours - Upon selecting the Hours the related fields will be displayed on the

The Scheduler of Hours is defined as: If user schedule for every hour then it will run for every 
hour starting from the start time between the start and end date.
- Advanced : If the user want to configure the cron expression, based on their requirement, 
they can use Advanced option. For the direct configuration user can use the other tabs ( Min‐
utes, Hours, Daily, Weekly, and Monthly).
For Example: if user wants to schedule on the 2nd day of every month January at 1 hour 30

Process Automation
Overview
Overview
Last updated on May 12, 2023
Process Automation refers to the use of technology and software to automate repetitive, manual, or 
rule-based tasks or processes in HyperSense. The goal of process automation is to reduce er‐
rors, improve efficiency, and free up human resources to focus on more value-added activities in 
HyperSense. Whenever customer face any issue, there should be a robust system that resolves the 
issue and provides the best customer experience. Benefits of process automation include increased 
efficiency, improved accuracy, reduced costs, faster processing times, enhanced compliance, and 
improved scalability. By automating routine tasks, organizations can optimize their operations, allo‐
cate resources more effectively, and improve overall productivity. For accurate and efficient au‐
tomation system, HyperSense ensures careful planning, analysis of existing processes, and consid‐
eration of potential impacts on system, customers, and stakeholders.
It identifies suitable processes with proper governance, control, and continually monitor and opti‐
mize automated processes to achieve the desired outcomes.
In HyperSense platform, you can make use of the Process Automation Studio to raise any concern/
issue by configuring a case template and then creating a case. Process Automation Studio is a tick‐
eting system that deals with the process of managing case instances generated by the case-gener‐
ating source. It provides a workflow environment that guides the Communication Service Providers
(CSPs) through the stages they need to perform to investigate, diagnose and resolve identified is‐
sues. It helps you in managing alerts effectively based on settings in workstep configuration.
Note:
How it works?
In HyperSense, generating a case for addressing an issue requires a case template. A case template 
is defined for any case instance, with the workflows to include corrective activities for resolving 
case instances. The workflows constitute a sequence of worsksteps that map directly to the deci‐
sion points from process flow charts. This case template can be attached to any of the case generat‐
ing sources, which will provide the flexibility to generate cases. A case is generated in two ways:
The case-generating source is any activity that can result in a discrepancy in the application. 
Example: KPI violation in BMS generates a case. Here, BMS is considered as case generating 
source.
•
Case Instances are managed in a workflow that has worksteps for resolving discrepancies.
•
Automatic Case Generation: A case is generated automatically if there is any violation in config‐
ured KPI values in BMS.

Last updated on May 12, 2023
Process Automation is a case management tool that efficiently manages cases or incidents in Hyper‐
Sense. Whenever customer face any issue, Process Automation acts as a robust system to resolve 
the identified issues and provide the best Customer Experience.
It provides a workflow environment that guides the communication service providers through the 
stages they need to diagnose, investigate, and resolve the identified cases. Diagnosis refers to cate‐
gorizing cases on the basis of domain and identifying anomalies. Investigation refers to analyzing, 
gathering evidence, and finding artefacts related to a case. Finally, resolving the case by providing a 
comprehensive report detailing the investigation process, findings, and recommended actions to be 
taken by concerned authorities.
In HyperSense, Process Automation supports the below domains: 
Below is the sequence of operations to create, investigate, and close the case:
Case Template Creation
The first step is to create a Case Template for the domain in which the issue is identified. Case tem‐
plate is a user-defined grouping of the common issues with properties and a workflow. Case tem‐
plates are defined with workflow for resolving case instances. To raise a case, first you need to con‐
figure the case template that resembles the case type. For example, if you need to raise a case relat‐
ed to Business Assurance, then it is required to configure a case template with Business Assurance
as case domain. Case Template configuration is done from workspace of Process Automation Stu‐
dio. For more information, see Case Template Creation.
Workstep Configuration
After creating a case template, the second step is to configure Workstep Configuration. A Workstep 
is an individual operation in the sequence of operations comprising a workflow. Each Workstep has 
prescribed properties that must be completed before completing a step. For more information, see 
Workstep Configuration Details.
Manual Case Generation: A case is generated manually with the case creation based on any dis‐
crepancies in KPI values.

crease asset handling across different teams and increase utilization

Alert Notifications in Process Automation
Alert Notifications are the message notifications that notifies you about specific events happen in 
Process Automation Studio. These notifications are triggered as per the configured rules in alert 
configuration when there is any data breach or deviation happens in the Process Automation.  You 
can configure the alert notifications in alerts configuration screen under common settings.  For more 
information on how to configure alerts and other relevant information, see Alerts Configuration. 
Different Types of Alerts in Process Automation
There are three types of alerts that are received in Process Automation.
Configured Example
Let us take an example of configuring an alert template. As you can see in the above image, you are 
creating an alert template based on New Cases. The selected time interval is 15 minutes. The select‐
ed measures under policy is Case Statistics - New Cases and policy condition is Cases in New State 
are greater than 10. After configuration, if you click Create, the alert template is created. Let us say, 
the alert template is created at 07:00 PM. Then from the time of creation of alert template, the sys‐
tem starts monitoring if any new cases are generated for the next 15 minutes (07:00 PM to 07:15 
PM) as configured, and triggers an alert if the number of new cases generated is greater than 10 for 
period of 07:00 PM to 07:15 PM. From 07:15 PM again system monitors the generation of new cases 
for the next 15 minutes, and triggers an alert if the number of new cases generated is greater than 10 
for period 07:15 PM to 07:30 PM. This time system never considers the cases that are generated be‐
fore 07:15 PM. This process continues.
Note:
Variables
Variables are the dynamic entities that store the information. While configuring any alert, variables 
store the real time dynamic values and display them in the alert message received.
Types of variables available for different types of alerts in Process Automation are:

Data Copier
Data copier copies the cumulative data of the CDR that violates the FM rules and alarms. When ever 
a case gets generated, the data with which it got violated or some data that passed through grouped

copied in resultant table. This helps the user to analyse the data easily. For a particular fraud case,

closed or expired.
The copy action works in two approaches:
Data Copier workflow
When an alarm is raised from BMS , then the respective case will be raised from Process Automation

that grouped entity with all related details. Then it enters into Kafka Queue, Consumer does the Job 
and copies the data for that particular grouped entity values raised as alarm and inserted into Sys‐
tem copier results table.  For the Current day copy and the upcoming days CDR of that grouped enti‐
ty will be copied by the Progressive Approach. A Local cache will be created for the Source Pipeline 
for the incoming CDR, whenever alarms generated there will be a update in the cache that we have 
configured, Which involves matching of lookup from the Meta table grouped entity values with the

Case Group Cards
Case Groups card in Dynamic/Auto case grouping provides an option to view the list of similar cases 
along with their groups in case investigation screen. This feature helps you to track and identify the 
list of similar cases with same grouped entity. You can quickly access the investigation screen of 
any other similar case by using comprehensive case investigation card from the case investigation 
screen of existing case. This facilitates the user to analyze the cases easily and take prompt action 
on all similar cases at a time by investigating, and closing them quickly. This feature is applicable on‐
ly to the cases of Fraud Management domain.
How Case Groups card works?
For example, if you configure Case Groups card with a grouped entity value in a case template and 
create a case, then it displays the list of case groups along with cases available in each group with 
same grouped entity value in the case group card under investigation screen. (If you select the case 
group, it list all the cases available with same Grouped Entity value and if you click the case, it navi‐
gates you to the investigation screen of that particular case).

Auto/Dynamic Case Grouping
In Process Automation, generally cases are located in either Grouped/Ungrouped Cases tab based 
on template configuration. Consider a scenario where there are 3 cases generated from 3 different 
templates on the same entity (say phonenumber). Now, when the analyst opens process automation, 
he needs to open the grouped Cases/ ungrouped Cases tab and select each case and then close 
those cases after analysis. If there is a way to group the cases based on Entity value, user can easily 
identify, analyse and close those cases. So this feature (Autogrouping) makes this grouping possi‐
ble. It is a way where cases in Process Automation will be grouped based on some rules configured 
and that group will be available in new tab called Dynamic grouped Cases tab.
If you select Close all similar cases option from case investigation screen, the Close All Case 
window is displayed. Configure the required options to close the cases and click Close All Cases
to close the cases.  For more information on closing the case at bulk, see Bulk case closure.

Case Re-Occurrence Count shows the count value when a case is reoccurred. If a new case is creat‐

Reverse Connection
Usually you can forward a case from one workstep to other workstep in forward direction. Reverse 
connection allow you connect a worksteps in the reverse direction.
To configure Reverse connection:
Basic Flow
Consider a template of multiple worksteps. connect the worksteps from start workflow to End 
workflow. To configure reverse connection, connect the required workstep to the previous 
workstep in reverse direction.

workflow.

If you try to configure the reverse connection from a workstep that is connected to end work‐
flow, then it displays an error. Here BMS_R3 is connected to end workflow. so you can not con‐
figure reverse connection for this workstep.

When the template is configured with approve reject workstep, you can connect the flow in for‐
ward and reverse direction.

Whenever a workstep is connected to more than 2 outgoing nodes forward or reverse, then you 
can configure conditional rules. Click conditional rule icon to configure the rules.

to configured workstep, if not, it comes back to default workstep.

port. The workstep BMS_R2-import is connected as reverse connection.

step is displayed. Investigate the workstep and enter the property values configured.

Escalation Validation Rules
Escalation Validation Rules are the set of rules to configure SLA(Service Level Agreement) time du‐
ration while escalating a case to next level.
The terms related to Escalation Validation Rules are+
Following are the escalation configuration rules:
Case template duration=Time duration to solve any case template.
1.
Workstep SLA= Time duration to solve the individual work step.
2.
Escalation SLA= Time duration to escalate workstep to next user.
3.
Pre-Escalation SLA= Certain duration before which Mail or SMS is sent before escalation. It 
should be less than escalation SLA.
4.
Case Template duration >= Workstep SLA>= Escalation SLA>= Pre-Escalation SLA.
1.
Workstep SLA should be >= Escalation SLA.
If you enter Escalation SLA value greater than or equal to Workstep SLA, it throws an error.
2.
Escalation SLA>= Pre-Escalation SLA. 
If you enter the Pre-Escalation SLA value greater than or equal to Escalation SLA, it throws an 
error.
3.
If Workstep SLA is not set, then Case Template duration >=Escalation SLA>=Pre-Escalation 
SLA.
4.
You can not reduce the Case Template Duration which is already set.
If you try to reduce the existing Case Template Duration, it displays the Save Configuration win‐
dow saying the pre-escalation alert will be disabled. In edit case scenario, if Case Template Du‐
ration< Worstep SLA then Workstep SLA = Case Template Duration. Escalation Duration = New 
Case Template Duration - New Case Template Duration * 0.75 (0.75 is a global variable and can 
be changed as per the requirement).

In Process Automation, generally cases are generated from BMS pipeline in which case operator is

Creating your First Dashboard
This section is focused on documentation for end-users who will be using BIS for the data analysis 
and exploration workflow (data analysts, business analysts, data scientists, etc).
This tutorial targets someone who wants to create charts and dashboards in BIS. We’ll show you 
how to connect BIS to a new database and configure a table in that database for analysis. You’ll also 
explore the data you’ve exposed and add a visualization to a dashboard so that you get a feel for the 
end-to-end user experience.
Connecting to a new database
BIS itself doesn't have a storage layer to store your data but instead pairs with your existing SQL-
speaking database or data store.
First things first, we need to add the connection credentials to your database to be able to query and 
visualize data from it.

Dataset option.

Chart Walkthrough
Business Intelligence Studio (BIS) provides a variety of charts that will help you visualize your data. 
To get a fast peek at all the alternatives, simply select + Chart in the Toolbar and filter by All Charts:
Types of Charts
Chart Name
Description

title: HyperSense User Guide
text:
Version:  2.5.13.5
© 2026 Subex - Confidential
Page 600
Area Chart
Shows how ratios, proportions, or percentages of a metric (or metrics) 
change over a dimension (like time) by utilizing the changing area beneath 
the lines.
Bar Chart
Bars show how a metric (or metrics) changes across a given dimension (time, 
for example).
Bar Chart (legacy) 
(Deprecated)
Bar charts offer a simple means of displaying category data visually.
Big Number
Showcases a single metric front-and-center. Big number is best used to call 
attention to a KPI or the one thing you want your audience to focus on.
Big Number with 
Trendline
Showcases a single number accompanied by a simple line chart, to call atten‐
tion to an important metric along with its change over time or other dimen‐
sion.
Box Plot
Also known as a box and whisker plot, this visualization compares the distrib‐
utions of a related metric across multiple groups. The box in the middle em‐
phasizes the mean, median, and inner 2 quartiles. The whiskers around each 
box visualize the min, max, range, and outer 2 quartiles.
Bubble Chart (lega‐
cy) (Deprecated)
Visualizes a metric across three dimensions of data in a single chart (X axis, 
Y axis, and bubble size). Bubbles from the same group can be showcased us‐
ing bubble color.
Bullet Chart
Showcases the progress of a single metric against a given target. The higher 
the fill, the closer the metric is to the target.
Calendar Heatmap
Visualizes how a metric has changed over a time using a color scale and a 
calendar view. Gray values are used to indicate missing values and the linear 
color scheme is used to encode the magnitude of each day's value.
Chord Diagram
Showcases the flow or link between categories using thickness of chords. 
The value and corresponding thickness can be different for each side.
Country Map
Visualizes how a single metric varies across a country's principal subdivi‐
sions (states, provinces, etc) on a choropleth map. Each subdivision's value 
is elevated when you hover over the corresponding geographic boundary.
Event Flow
Compares the lengths of time different activities take in a shared timeline 
view.
Funnel Chart
Uses the physical funnel's component thickness to illustrate the various 
pipeline stages in your business.
Showcases how a metric changes as the funnel progresses. This classic 
chart is useful for visualizing drop-off between stages in a pipeline or lifecy‐
cle.

title: HyperSense User Guide
text:
Version:  2.5.13.5
© 2026 Subex - Confidential
Page 601
Gauge Chart
This sort of chart illustrates partial progress towards a certain number by 
reusing gauges from industrial and scientific settings.
Graph Chart
Uses nodes, or circles, and edges, or connected lines, between nodes to vi‐
sualize connected items or events.
Line Chart
Line chart is used to visualize measurements taken over a given category. 
Line chart is a type of chart which displays information as a series of data 
points connected by straight line segments. It is a basic type of chart com‐
mon in many fields.
Mixed Chart
Using a common X-axis, combine several visualizations into a single chart 
container.
Pie Chart
A pie-shaped statistical chart that displays the percentage of various data 
shown as slices inside a circle.
Pivot Table
A table with grouped values that collects each item from a larger table into 
one or more distinct categories.
Radar Chart
You can see a parallel collection of measurements for several groups or cate‐
gories with a radar chart.
Sankey Diagram
A flow diagram where the size of the flow lines from a source to a target rep‐
resents the relative size of the metric data.
Scatter Plot
Scatter Plot has the horizontal axis in linear units, and the points are connect‐
ed in order. It shows a statistical relationship between two variables.
Smooth Line
Smooth-line is a variation of the line chart. Without angles and hard edges, 
Smooth-line sometimes looks smarter and more professional.
Stepped Line Chart
A line chart variation where two data points are connected by 90-degree 
stepped lines.
Stepped-line graph (also called step chart) is a variation of line chart but with 
the line forming a series of steps between data points. A step chart can be 
useful when you want to show the changes that occur at irregular intervals.
Time-Series Per‐

Rolling Mean
There is quite a lot of variation in the data, which makes it difficult to identify any trend. One ap‐
proach we can take is to show instead a rolling average of the time series. To do this, in the Data tab 
go to Advanced Analytics, select mean in the Rolling box and enter 7 into both Periods and Min Peri‐
ods. The period is the length of the rolling period expressed as a multiple of the Time Grain. In our 
example, the Time Grain is day, so the rolling period is 7 days, such that on the 7th October 2023 the 
value shown would correspond to the first seven days of October 2023. Lastly, by specifying Min 
Periods as 7, we ensure that our mean is always calculated on 7 days and we avoid any ramp up pe‐
riod.
After displaying the chart by selecting Update Chart you will see that the data is less variable and 
that the series starts later as the ramp up period is excluded.
Save the chart as Tutorial Rolling Mean and add it to the Tutorial Dashboard.

In this section, we will compare values in our time series to the value a week before. Start off by 
opening the Tutorial Advanced Analytics Base chart, by going to Charts in the top menu and then se‐
lecting the visualization name in the list (alternatively, find the chart in the Tutorial Dashboard and

Row Level Security
Row Level Security (RLS) rules limit which rows of your data can be accessed by specific groups of 
users. Functionally, this means that a WHERE clause is added to all queries on a specific set of data for 
a particular set of users. These users will only be able to view certain rows of your data. You can ap‐
ply Row Level Security to all workspaces roles. 
You can either specify a group of users whose queries to be limited by the rule (or) you can specify 
a group of users whose queries not to be limited by the rule.

text:

© 2026 Subex - Confidential
Page 689
Data Management handles the ETL process which stands for extract, transform, and load. It is com‐
monly used to extract data from various sources, transform it into a suitable format, and load it into a 
target destination. The ETL process ensures that data is standardized, and organized for effective 
analysis and reporting.
DMS integrates with a variety of data sources to help you poll the data, transform it into readable for‐
mat, load it into a destination system of your choice. It offers you numerous ways to fetch the data, 
such as streaming data, data stored at cloud spaces (GCS, Amazon, Azure), ingesting from the data‐
base table, reading flat files (.xml, .json, .csv, binary, .txt, ASCII, ASN.1 etc), reading workbooks 
(.xls, .xlsx, .xlsb etc). Data is transformed into required format using various transformation opera‐
tors. Transformed data is stored in various data sinks which can be further used for analysis and re‐
porting.
Below is the sequence of operation to create and configure a ETL pipeline in HyperSense.
Create Pipeline
The first step is to Create Pipeline. A Pipeline moves your data from a Source system to a Destination 
database or data warehouse. It represents the end-to-end process of extracting data from various 
sources, transforming it into a desired format, and loading it into a target system or database. Multi‐
ple Pipelines may load to the same Destination. For more information, see Create a Pipeline.
Data Source
The next step is to configure a Data Source : A Data Source can be a database or a file storage which 
has the data that you want to analyze. In this step of ETL processing, data is extracted from one or 
more source systems. Extraction involves querying the source systems, retrieving relevant data, and 
bringing it to a staging area for further processing. HyperSense integrates with a variety of Sources 
including databases, files, message queues, or other data repositories which are explained below: 
Relational databases : Data can be extracted from database systems such as Postgres. The ETL 
process connects to the database, executes queries, and retrieves the required data. It supports 
following database: RDBMS, MySQL, MSSQL, Oracle, Postgres. For more information about data 
base configuration, refer to RDBMS.
•
File System : Data can be sourced from files in formats like CSV (comma-separated values), Excel 
spreadsheets, JSON (JavaScript Object Notation), XML (eXtensible Markup Language), or log 
files. The ETL pipeline reads the files and extracts the relevant information. For more information 
about files configuration, refer to FTP, SFTP, File Sorting, Email, and Local File.
•
Cloud storage : Data can be stored in cloud-based storage systems like Amazon S3, Google 
Cloud Storage, Azure Blob Storage or Hive. The ETL pipeline connects to these storage systems, 
accesses the data files, and performs the extraction. For more information about cloud storage 
configuration, refer to Amazon S3, Google Cloud Storage, Azure Blob Storage or Hive.
•
Message queues: Some ETL pipelines may source data from message queues such as Apache 
Kafka. The pipeline consumes messages from the queue and processes the data they contain. In 
real-time or near-real-time ETL scenarios, data sources can be streaming platforms like Apache 
Kafka. The pipeline continuously processes data as it arrives. For more information about mes‐
sage brokers configuration, refer to Kafka.
•

title: HyperSense User Guide
text:
Version:  2.5.13.5
© 2026 Subex - Confidential
Page 690
Transformation Operator
In the third step of the pipeline configuration, you need to configure Transformation Operator. A 
Transformation Operator refers to a component that performs data cleansing, validation, normaliza‐
tion, aggregation, enrichment on the data as it moves through the pipeline. These operators are re‐
sponsible for transforming the data from its source format to a desired format, applying various op‐
erations or calculations, and preparing it for further processing or loading into the target system. Da‐
ta transformation operators in HyperSense can perform a wide range of tasks, including:
Parser: The first basic step of transformation is Parsing the data by adding a Parser and configur‐
ing it. These operators divide or parse complex data structures into smaller, more manageable 
components. For example, they can split a text string into separate fields or extract specific ele‐
ments from a nested JSON structure. HyperSense offers the intuitive and easy-to-use interface, 
where you can apply transformations on the data till you reach the final data model that is re‐
quired for your business reporting and intelligence needs. Below parser type is supported in Hy‐
perSense:
•
Data File Parser(ASCII)
1.
Data File Parser(ASN.1)
2.
Data File Parser(Binary)
3.
Data File Parser (CSV)
4.
Data File Parser (XLS/XLSX/XLSB)
5.
Data File Parser (XML)
6.
Mapping: Schema Mapper helps you map your Source schemas to tables in your Destination 
(Sink). Mapping operators transform data values from one representation or format to another. 
They can be used to standardize data formats, convert data types, or map values from different 
source systems into a unified format. Mapping Operators perform calculations or apply transfor‐
mations to modify data values or derive new attributes. This includes mathematical operations, 
date/time manipulations, string manipulations, and other custom transformations. Mapping opera‐
tor also acts as a Aggregation operators that combines multiple data records into a single record 
or summarize data based on specific criteria. Examples include calculating sums, averages, 
counts, or other statistical measures. For more information on detailed configuration, see Map‐
ping.
•
Filtering: The operator selects or filters specific data records or attributes based on defined crite‐
ria. This allows for the extraction of relevant data while discarding unnecessary information. For 
more information detailed configuration, see Filtering.
•
Joining and Merging: Joining and merging operators combine data from multiple sources based 
on common keys or attributes. They enable the consolidation of data from different tables or 
datasets into a single dataset for further processing. For more information on detailed configura‐
tion, see Joining and Merging, and LDC.
•
Data Enrichment: Data enrichment operators enhance the data by adding additional information 
from external sources. This can involve retrieving and integrating data from databases, or refer‐
ence datasets to augment the existing data. For more information on detailed configuration, 
see Data Enrichment.
•

title: HyperSense User Guide
text:
Version:  2.5.13.5
© 2026 Subex - Confidential
Page 691
Data Sink
The last step is to configure a Destination (Sink). Sink refers to a destination or target where data is 
written or stored after undergoing transformations or processing. It is the endpoint or final destina‐
tion for data in a data flow pipeline. The data is typically persisted in a format suitable for long-term 
storage or further analysis. There are several types of Data Sinks commonly used in HyperSense da‐
ta processing pipelines:
Deploy and Run
Deploy: The deployment phase involves the setup and configuration of the data pipeline infrastruc‐
ture, tools, and resources required to execute the pipeline. During this stage, the pipeline architec‐
ture is defined, and the necessary components, such as data processing engines, storage systems, 
and computing resources, are provisioned and interconnected.
Run: The running phase involves the execution and monitoring of the deployed data pipeline. Once 
the infrastructure is set up and the pipeline is deployed, it starts processing data according to the 
defined workflow. During the run phase, data is ingested, transformed, and analyzed based on the 
predefined tasks and processing logic.
Relational Database: Relational databases, such as Postgres are commonly used as Data Sinks. 
Data can be stored in tables with predefined schemas, allowing for efficient querying and struc‐
tured data storage. For more information about data base configuration RDBMS Sink.
•
Message Queueing Systems: Message queuing systems like Apache Kafka can act as Data Sinks 
when the focus is on real-time streaming or event-based data processing. Data is written to top‐
ics or queues for consumption by downstream systems or applications. For more information 
about message brokers configuration, refer to Kafka.
•
Cloud Data Lakes: Cloud-based data lakes, such as Amazon S3, Azure Blob Storage, 
S3Presto, Hadoop Distributed File System (HDFS), Azure Blob Storage Trino, Hive, offer scalable 
and cost-efficient storage for both structured and unstructured data. Data Sinks like data lakes 
provide a flexible and schema-on-read approach, enabling data exploration and analysis. For 
more information about cloud storage configuration, refer to Amazon S3, Azure Blob Storage, 
S3Presto, Hadoop Distributed File System (HDFS), Azure Blob Storage Trino, Hive, Google Cloud 
Storage (GCS), GCS Trino.
•
Cache Sink: Distributed cache refers to a caching mechanism that spans multiple nodes or ma‐
chines in a distributed system. It is designed to improve the performance and scalability of appli‐
cations by storing frequently accessed data in memory closer to the application or service that re‐
quires it. In a distributed cache, data is partitioned and distributed across multiple cache nodes or 
servers. Each node holds a portion of the cached data, and together, they form a distributed 
cache cluster. When an application needs to access a piece of data, it first checks if it exists in 
the local cache of the node it is running on. If the data is not present locally, the cache system re‐
trieves it from a remote cache node within the cluster. For more information on configuration of 
Cache Sink, see Cache Sink.
•

schedule the pipeline in order to deploy it to a desired deployment frequency.

Clone Pipeline
Last updated on May 12, 2023
Clone Pipeline refers to creating a copy or duplicate of an active version pipeline. This replicates the 
structure, configuration, and functionality of the active version pipeline. The purpose of creating a 
clone of a pipeline is to test new changes with different data sources. Here, the approach is to re‐
duce the effort by reusing transformation logic. The cloned pipeline could also be used to restore the 
pipeline during production, ensuring data flow. This allows parallel execution, increasing processing 
capacity and speeding up data processing.
To copy and save a pipeline with different name:

Cache setting is a global settings to store the cache data locally. It's helpful for providing requests 
for data that is static or changes infrequently. The caching settings can refresh the cache at a speci‐
fied frequency. You can configure multiple cache to a single table, and one cache for multiple tables.
To add a cache settings:

data value.

String Rule Settings
Last updated on May 19, 2025
String Rule Settings allows you to create the set of rules that operate on string elements for matching 
purpose. You can define the output when string is matched and when it is not matched.
To configure String Rule Settings:
Minutes: Allows you to enter the file collection time interval in minutes and seconds. For example, 
if you want system to collect file at every 5 minutes and 30 seconds, then configure as: Every 5 
minute(s) on 30 SS.
•
Hourly: Allows you to enter the file collection time interval in Hours, Minutes, and Seconds. For 
example, if you want system to collect file at every 2 hours, then configure as: Every 2 Hour(s) on 
0 MM on 0 SS.
•
Daily: Allows you to enter the file collection time interval in a day.
•
Every :Every nth day, where n can be up to 5. Example: if you have selected Every as 2, then 
on every alternate day, file collection will be triggered.
◦
Every Working day: By default, Monday to Friday is considered as Working days in the system.
◦
Weekly: Allows you to enter the file collection time interval and define the trigger day(s) of the 
week. For example, if you want system to collect file on every Monday at every 11 pm, then con‐
figure as: Select Monday checkbox, at 23 HH on 0 MM on 0 SS.
•
Monthly: Allows you to enter the file collection time interval in week or day of a particular month. 
For example, If you want to set the collection time as 3rd March at 22:00:00 or on the first work‐
ing day of March, then configure as following:
•
On the 3rd day of every 3 Month at 22 HH 00 MM 00 SS 
◦
On the First Monday of 3 Month at  22 HH 00 MM 00 SS
◦
Yearly: Allows you to enter the file collection time interval in a year on a particular month. For ex‐
ample, If you want to set the collection time as 27th February at 23:59:59 or on the 3rd Sunday 
of February of every year then configure as following.
•
Every February on the 27th day at 23 HH 59 MM 59 SS
◦
On the Third Sunday of February at  23 HH 59 MM 59 SS
◦
Scheduler expression: Displays the time value in expression according to the configured settings.
•
In the DMS landing page or pipeline canvas page, click settings icon  > Open String Rule Set‐
tings.

This feature enables user to create a customized Jar as per their requirement which is suitable to

10.
Enter the required rule.
For example, if you define rule like "(91)(765)(.*)". The first string entry is (91). The second sting 
entry is (765). The third string entry is a variable (.*) and can be any number. Let us assume (.*)
as 123. If you give $1 in output field, it returns 91 as output.
If you give $2, then it returns 765 as output. If you give $3, then it returns 123 as output. 
If you give $1$2, then it returns 91765" as output.
If you give 0$3, then it returns "0765" as output. 
For example, if you define a rule like "(....123)(765)(456)". The first string entry is (....123), that 
means it takes first four number as any number before 123. The second string entry is (765). 
The third string entry is (456).
Let us assume the sample number "1234123987689" for validation.
In this case,  If you give $1 in output field, it returns 1234123 as it satisfies the match key format 
(....123).
If you give $2, then it returns 765 as output. If you give $3, then it returns 456 as output. 
11.
If there is no match happened. Then you need to select Non Match Steps.
Consider an example of no match happened. In this case, select a specific rule number un‐
der Non Match Steps drop-down so that it checks for next set of rule available. If there is no oth‐
er rule available, then it returns Null as output.
Let us assume if you select 2 under Non Match Steps drop-down. It validates rule 2 and gives 
the appropriate output.
Similarly you can add as many rules as per your requirement. Click Done to save your configura‐
tion.
12.
To apply the string rules, see Mapping section.

In Pipeline Repository window, there are two versions: Current and Latest. Current version

version generated from the last created version.
•

number. For any pipeline that is newly created, imported or cloned, Current Version and Lat‐
est Version is always same i.e., 1.0.

For example: If there are 3 versions for a pipeline - 1.0, 2.0, and 3.0. Out of 3 versions, Active 
version is 2.0. Then Current Version is 2.0 and Latest Version is 3.0. If you create new ver‐
sion, then Latest Version will be 4.0.

By default, Priority is set to 1. If you give priority value as one, one number of threads are al‐
located to the pipeline. The more number of threads you allocate to a pipeline, the more it 
perform the tasks faster. When you prioritize a pipeline with the priority value as 10, then

can take various forms depending on the specific ETL pipeline implementation. Below types are the

To configure Data Source:
After providing priority, Back Pressure and Queue Memory, if we click on done button in sched‐

Relational databases : Data can be extracted from database systems such as Oracle or Postgres. 
The ETL process connects to the database, executes queries, and retrieves the required data.
•
File System : Data can be sourced from files in formats like CSV (comma-separated values), Excel 
spreadsheets, JSON (JavaScript Object Notation), XML (eXtensible Markup Language), or log 
files. The ETL pipeline reads the files and extracts the relevant information.
•
Cloud storage : Data can be stored in cloud-based storage systems like Amazon S3, Google 
Cloud Storage, or Azure Blob Storage or Hive. The ETL pipeline connects to these storage sys‐
tems, accesses the data files, and performs the extraction.
•
Message queues: Some ETL pipelines may source data from message queues such as Apache 
Kafka. The pipeline consumes messages from the queue and processes the data they contain.
•
Streaming platforms: In real-time or near-real-time ETL scenarios, data sources can be streaming 
platforms like Apache Kafka. The pipeline continuously processes data as it arrives.
•
Remote File Storage: FTP and SFTP
•
Cloud Storage: Hive, S3, GCS and Azure Blob Storage
•
Message Brokers: Kafka
•
SQL Database: RDBMS, MySQL, MSSQL, Oracle, Postgres

File Integrity tab is used to check the data integrity and data quality.
In this tab, File Sequence Check is configured. File Sequence Check is the process of checking

duplicate even though the pipeline has two files with the same file names.

File Sorting
Last updated on September 6, 2024
File Sorting is Data Source used to sort the incoming CDR based on the Timestamp to handle out of 
sequence records. It uses two pipelines. First Pipeline is used to fetch the incoming CDR and store 
the data in Local File Sink. Second Pipeline is used to fetch the records stored in Local File sink, ap‐
ply sorting to out of sequence records and use ARC to calculate the benefit. Calculated result is 
stored in sink. Data table result can be viewed in the Data Catalog.
File Sorting data source is configured for pipelines that has sink as Local File Sink. Record is fetched 
from local directory, sorting is applied for out of sequence records and rate benefit is calculated us‐
ing ARC operator.
